record.name: Helen Diller Family Cancer Research Building
names: Helen Diller Family Cancer Research Building
record.summary: A cancer research building of about 164,000 sq ft (SFGate, May 2009; sources differ, see facts) of two interlocking L-shaped, five-story wings (one for wet labs, one for PI/fellow offices), which broke ground in 2006 and opened in June 2009. The exact opening day is not confirmed: SFGate announced on May 31, 2009 that the building would open on Tuesday (June 2), and its June 2, 2009 design column calls it 'the new Helen Diller Family Cancer Research Building'.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL -- OpenStreetMap building footprint (crowd-mapped, not an official survey), not a hand trace or plan estimate. This is the opposite situation from Mission Bay's condo-mapped residential towers (Avalon, Radiance, etc.): here, ONE large Assessor land parcel spans SEVERAL UCSF buildings (in DataSF's Assessor parcel data the active lot 8711509 is about 12.2 acres by its drawn outline (the Assessor roll lists it at 555 Mission Bay Blvd with a lot area of 528,539 sq ft, about 12.1 acres) and contains this building together with the Hearst Tower, North and West buildings), so using the parcel boundary per building would make multiple records overlap and double-count the same ground. The real building footprint is the only non-overlapping, honest shape for each one.

facts.value: Two interlocking L-shaped wings: one wet-lab wing, one PI/fellow office wing

costs.what: SFGate (May 31, 2009, ahead of the building's grand opening) calls it the "$135 million Helen Diller Family Cancer Research Building"; the article does not say whether the figure is a cost, a budget or a construction cost. It adds that Helen Diller and her husband "contributed $35 million to build the center"

Images: no plan drawing, elevation or openly-licensed photograph was found for this building specifically. Searched: UCSF Real Estate's Mission Bay campus-site and LRDP pages (realestate.ucsf.edu, which could not be checked); the UCSF 2014 LRDP EIR's CEQAnet filing (SCH 2013092047, whose pre-2016 attachments aren't hosted on CEQAnet itself); a May 2000 Regents Committee on Grounds and Buildings design-approval item for an early Mission Bay building (text-only, no figures); the 2008 "UCSF Mission Bay Planning Principles" appendix (a citywide-scale community map, no individual buildings labeled); and a UCSF wayfinding campus map (not an adopted plan, EIR or permit filing, so not eligible as public-record even though found). Not pursued further; the record's own project sources above remain the citation for the building's history.

As of 2026-09-29, the UCSF 2009 news release (which could not be checked) is the only source for the grand opening as an event; SFGate's May 31, 2009 article says the building 'officially opens Tuesday' (June 2, 2009) and was written after staff had moved in, and is now cited as well. The size is unresolved: SFGate says nearly 164,000 sq ft, the architect's page says 174,020 (units mislabelled), and 161,757 plus 20,000 sq ft of vivarium space was not found in a readable source.

Update 2026-10-12, opening date: the opening is shown at month level. UCSF's release "UCSF Celebrates Grand Opening of Helen Diller Family Cancer Research Building at Mission Bay" (ucsf.edu/news/2009/06/4248), the only source for the grand opening as an event, refused access, as did three other UCSF, Tradeline and GenomeWeb pages that report on it. The readable sources are SFGate on May 31, 2009 (before the event: "officially opens Tuesday"), SFGate on June 2, 2009 (calls the building "new") and Wikipedia ("opened in June 2009", itself citing SFGate), so the exact day is not confirmed.
The $135 million figure comes from a single press article that uses it as a descriptor of the building and does not say what it measures; no second source or permit value was found to compare.

Gross floor area: SFGate (May 31, 2009) calls it a 'nearly 164,000-square-foot' building; the architect's page (Rafael Viñoly Architects, undated) lists a size of 174,020 with a units label ('gross square meters') that cannot be right for this building.
